clue.text: Being infectious, catch shopper

parts.note: someone infectious who passes on a disease is a carrier
to catch or capture something is to bag it

explanation.surface: Someone who is infectious manages to catch a passing shopper.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopper is the British name for a large bag used for carrying purchases from the shops.

clue.text: Dog's tail at the end may

definitions.text: Dog's tail at the end may

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog; the possessive adds no letter

indicators.note: at the end picks out only the final letter of the word tail

explanation.surface: A remark about what a dog's tail may do at its tip.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a dog's tail may curl at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Many dogs' tails twist round into a coil at their tip, which is the verb sense meant.

clue.text: Register on which one is regularly successful

definitions.meaning: a register or list of names, as in a class or electoral list

definitions.text: on which one is regularly successful
definitions.meaning: enjoying a run of repeated success

explanation.definitionFit: A roll is a list of names, and the idiom 'on a roll' means having a run of successes.

clue.text: Turn up and wildly berate spineless creature

parts.note: to turn something upside down is to invert it

indicators.note: wildly says the letters of berate are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone turns up and berates a feeble, spineless person wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal without a backbone is literally spineless, so the definition is a literal description.

clue.text: Hastily prepare — to come sec-end?

definitions.meaning: to ... a garment or meal is to make it quickly
the runner-up comes second, the hyphen being only a line break in the printed clue

explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'sec-end' is just 'second' split across a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Running something up means making it quickly, and finishing as runner-up means coming second.

clue.text: Casualties lying here as long train crashed

indicators.note: crashed suggests the letters of long train are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Victims of a train crash are laid out on the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Arlington National Cemetery in Virginia is where many American war dead are buried.

clue.text: Nitrogen fixed in blue grains

indicators.note: fixed in says the element is set inside the other word

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling sad
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: Nitrogen is fixed into blue-coloured grains of fertiliser.
explanation.definitionFit: Sand consists of tiny grains of rock, so grains describes it as a mass.

clue.text: A very small plot, almost infested with insect —— not popular

indicators.note: infested with says the insect gets inside the rest
almost says the last letter of the word is lost

parts.note: a garden is a small plot of land
the ant is a familiar insect

explanation.surface: A tiny garden plot crawling with insects is not a popular place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very' is the usual V; the dash before 'not popular' just separates wordplay from the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Avant-garde art is experimental, ahead of mainstream taste and so not popular.

clue.text: Yard moves to arrest me with fixed unit of size

indicators.note: to arrest is to hold, so these letters close round the next word
moves says the letters of yard shift into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
something fixed or certain is sure

explanation.surface: Scotland Yard moves to arrest me over a fixed matter.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard is the London police headquarters, which makes 'arrest' feel natural in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry measure is a system of units for the volume of goods like grain.

clue.text: Rally event organised avoiding diversions

indicators.note: organised says the letters of the phrase are arranged into order

explanation.surface: A motor rally is organised so as to avoid any road diversions.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking pertinently means staying on the point without digressing.

clue.text: Crazy unknown, no particular one

parts.note: Z is a mathematical unknown, like x and y
any means whichever one, with none in particular

explanation.surface: A mad unknown person, nobody in particular.
explanation.definitionFit: Zany means comically eccentric, which is a synonym of crazy.

clue.text: Shaggy little creature argued about book

parts.note: a beetle is a small insect
to row is to argue, so rowed means argued

explanation.surface: A shaggy little animal argued over a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Beetle-browed describes someone with shaggy, overhanging eyebrows.

clue.text: One approached casually, but having run in make to hit leg and middle

indicators.note: in after having run says the run letter goes inside the word for make

parts.note: to make something is to do it
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
pin is informal for leg
the middle is the centre

explanation.surface: A bowler runs in, trying to hit the leg and middle stumps.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket 'leg and middle' is a batting guard and stump target; here they are just PIN and CENTRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop-in centre is a facility people visit informally without an appointment.

clue.text: Returning from Mars, or unable to get there?

definitions.meaning: a craft returning from Mars is heading for Earth
something stuck on our planet cannot reach Mars

explanation.definitionFit: Earthbound means both heading towards our planet and confined to it, unable to leave.

clue.text: I send page with a kiss, received by chief man mistakenly

indicators.note: received by means taken inside the other letters
mistakenly says the letters of chief man are put in the wrong order

parts.note: X is the symbol for a kiss

explanation.surface: A love note with a kiss is mistakenly received by the chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistakenly' turns CHIEF MAN into FMACHINE; 'received by' puts AX after its F.
explanation.definitionFit: A fax machine transmits pages, so the device could say it sends a page.

clue.text: Member of institute has a half in shed

indicators.note: in places the half inside the other word

parts.note: a snake casts or sheds its skin
demi is a prefix meaning half

explanation.surface: An academic has half his time spent in a garden shed.
explanation.definitionFit: An academist is a member of an academy, a learned institute.

clue.text: One new coin I have taken for carrot

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a cent is a small coin
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone takes a new coin in return for a carrot.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrot is a reward dangled to motivate, in contrast to the stick.

clue.text: Drops features, being at end of budget

indicators.note: being at says the features come next to that letter
end of picks out only the final letter of the word budget

parts.note: ears are features of the head

explanation.surface: A budget sees some features dropped at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Tears are drops of liquid from the eyes.

clue.text: Plant a marigold, a little flower

indicators.note: a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Planting a marigold, a little flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' means something that flows: a river. The Tamar divides Devon and Cornwall in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A river flows, so in crosswords a flower is a river, and this one is in south-west England.

clue.text: Constituency's first on offer one may win

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the word constituency

parts.note: a tender is a formal offer

explanation.surface: A constituency's first-choice candidate on offer is one who may win.
explanation.definitionFit: A contender is a rival in the running who could possibly come out on top.

clue.text: One way to get Old Testament character living the simple life

annotationWithheld.why: One way to get Old Testament character living the simple life (4,2,6): a reverse clue whose reading (BACK TO = OT, NATURE = character) spans a 3-word phrase, refused as reversePhrase, while the cd form is refused as a downgrade of the reverse tree already filed
annotationWithheld.clue: One way to get Old Testament character living the simple life

clue.text: Facial ornament may be painful after a time

indicators.note: after places the pain behind the time

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to ache is to be painful

explanation.surface: A moustache might become painful after a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Tache is informal British for a moustache, a decoration on the face.

clue.text: Stink as this gun is brought to church

indicators.note: the gun brought to church makes the stink, so the church letters come off the stink

parts.note: a stench is a stink

explanation.surface: A gun brought into a church makes a stink.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says STEN plus CH is a stink, so take CH away from STENCH; the Sten was a British submachine gun.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sten was a cheap British submachine gun of the Second World War.

clue.text: Release a trio of Cockneys?

indicators.note: Cockneys are said to pronounce th as f

parts.note: a trio is three

explanation.surface: Release three Londoners.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, are stereotypically said to replace 'th' with 'f'.
explanation.definitionFit: To release a captive is to set them free.

clue.text: One going to marry shortly

indicators.note: shortly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to marry is to unite

explanation.surface: Someone is going to get married soon.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single thing, one item.

clue.text: Who out of your children (Spooner said) is proverbially dull?

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: which asks who out of a group
a daughter is one of your children

explanation.surface: A Spooner asks which of your children is notoriously dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Which daughter?' asks who of your children; swapping the opening sounds gives 'ditch water'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull as ditchwater is the stock British phrase for something extremely boring.

clue.text: Owed pounds in honourable affair

parts.note: money due is owed
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: Money owed in pounds in a gentleman's affair.
explanation.definitionFit: A duel was the formal fight to settle an affair of honour.

clue.text: Write about death in the last month by drug addiction

indicators.note: by places the drug next to the rest
in places these letters inside the month

parts.note: December is the last month, abbreviated

indicators.note: about means the writing goes round the death

parts.note: to pen is to write
end means death
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone writes about a death in December from drug addiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'death' as END is a common crossword equivalence; DEC is the standard abbreviation for December.
explanation.definitionFit: Dependence on a drug is addiction to it.
